reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) discusses mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms (twinning, phase transformation) in CoCrFeMnNi and CrCoNi alloys but provides no data or calculations on the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy, its SFE, or the effect of Co removal on SFE and twinning. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Removing Co from CoCrFeMnNi increases the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the FeNiCrMn alloy
Increased SFE suppresses deformation twinning in the Co-free alloy
Suppressed twinning shifts deformation mechanism to dislocation-mediated slip
Dislocation mobility in the Co-free alloy is temperature- and rate-dependent, leading to strengthening at low T/high rate and enhanced ductility at high T/low rate
The Co-free alloy will show a steeper yield strength increase with decreasing T/increasing rate and lower twin fractions compared to the equiatomic baseline
